title: Development
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers staff training and development; the closest, managing change well, only mentions training as one part of bringing people through change.

draft.title: Development
card: Training and development build the skills and knowledge of staff. Training is aimed at skills for a worker's current job. Development prepares staff for future roles.
an introduction for new workers. It covers the workplace, its policies, safety rules and the people they will work with.
learning while doing the work, such as coaching or shadowing an experienced worker. Off the job training happens away from the work, such as a course run by an outside provider.

Development programs, such as mentoring or management courses, prepare staff to take on more responsibility. A business may also gain from better skills, higher productivity and staff who stay longer.
draft.remember: Training builds skills for the present job. Development prepares staff for future roles.

a.q: Which activity is an example of induction?
opts: A new worker is shown the safety rules and meets the team
A worker attends an outside course on advanced accounting
A senior worker is coached to become a future manager
A worker learns a new machine by practising at their station
a.why: Induction introduces new workers to the business, its rules and its people. The outside course is off the job training, and coaching for management is development. Learning a machine at the station is on the job training, not an introduction to the workplace.
a.clue: Induction happens when someone is new to the business.

b.q: Priya has run a bakery in Bathurst for years. She sends her best baker, Tom, on a leadership program so he can later manage a second shop. What is this?
opts: Development, as it prepares Tom for a future role
Induction, as it is an introduction to a new role
Training only, as it builds skills for his current job
Maintenance, as it is a reward to keep Tom
b.why: The program prepares Tom for a future management role, so it is development. It is not induction, because Tom is not new to the business. It does not build skills for his present baking job, so it is not training only.
b.clue: Is the program about Tom's current job or a later one?

a.best: A new worker is shown the safety rules and meets the team

b.best: Development, as it prepares Tom for a future role
